summary: Pairing surface implemented per blueprint; contract-check ok, all 7 verify commands passed, AC-1..AC-7 collated clause by clause. Three latent, non-blocking robustness notes.
notes: contract-check ok=true, violations=[]; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (reviewed by hand, see below). 11/11 files, 1040/-11 lines vs max_diff_lines 1500; every per_class budget respected (largest headroom use: emparejar.rs 272/300, tests/emparejamiento.rs 305/390, adaptador.rs 118/250).

acceptance-coverage reports one gap: AC-6 has no blueprint test_scenario. Already triaged in 07-trace.json as false_gap_by_design (LES-2026-08-12-000000030: doc-presence criteria are verified by review). Collated by hand instead: STATUS.md appends one Definido entry dated 2026-08-13 / HEX-024 / task 4 of A-3 / FR-12 recording the pull-forward from A-6 by explicit human decision of 2026-08-13, and edits only the still-open Pendiente entry to record the local surface while keeping the remote A-6 surface pending; runbook-canal-fase-a.md touches only section 3, replacing the operator-gap caveat with the new mode plus an explicit remote-surface-pending note. Spanish, absolute dates, no mass-sending vocabulary introduced, no claim that Fase B replaces the sidecar.

Correlation lifecycle verified: the terminal-acuse path take()s the slot inside leer_mensajes before forwarding, so the Ok(acuse) return leaves nothing registered; timeout and channel-closed paths clear the slot explicitly; connection loss is deliberately subsumed by the same plazo, exactly as blueprint step 5 and the HEX-021 respaldo precedent prescribe. Orphan codigo/acuse are logged and dropped with the connection intact (tested end to end via a follow-up evento/confirmacion exchange).

LATENT DEFECT (not reachable by any in-tree caller, no fix required for this task): AdaptadorWhatsmeow::ordenar_emparejamiento overwrites the single pending slot without checking it is empty, so a second concurrent call silently clobbers the first. The clobbered waiter then observes rx.recv()==None and unconditionally sets the slot to None, de-registering the SECOND, still-live flow, which afterwards can only fail at its plazo while its codigo/acuse are logged as orphans. HEX-021's keyed respaldo map is immune because it removes by identificador_de_ronda. Today every caller (CLI ejecutar, both test suites) builds its own adapter and runs one sequential flow, and the normal cell mode never calls the method, so the path is unreachable. Suggested hardening for a future task: reject a second call while the slot is occupied, and clear the slot on exit only when it still holds this flow's own sender.

MINOR: the CodigoEmparejamiento dispatch arm uses `let _ = tx.send(..).await`, so a send failure on a vanished channel is dropped silently; blueprint step 4 asked for log-and-drop in that case. Observability only.

MINOR: emparejar::ejecutar maps checked_sub exhaustion (connection established but plazo already spent) to ErrorModoEmparejar::ConexionNoEstablecida, which mislabels a timeout as a connection failure; the timeout test consequently has to accept either error variant.

Fail-closed semantics match the blueprint exactly and differ from HEX-021 on purpose: an unrecognized resultado is logged and dropped WITHOUT touching the pending slot, and a test proves a later valid completado still resolves the same in-flight call. Typed translation lives one layer up in hexcell::emparejar with a defensive catch-all arm.

Stream honesty verified: one deadline computed once (tokio::time::Instant::now() + plazo) and consumed with timeout_at, never reset by an arriving code, so a rotating QR cannot keep the mode alive forever; rotation order asserted at both layers; expira_en_ms is a Unix-ms timestamp per protocol section 6, printed as such when non-zero and as 'Expiracion: desconocida' when 0.

No tautologies: mensajes.rs declares no wire-literal constants (only VERSION_PROTOCOLO), so the hardcoded tipo strings match the existing ordenar_respaldo_sqlstore precedent byte for byte. Test assertions read either structs the double parsed from the adapter's real serialization or the raw wire line the adapter wrote, never a test-local copy compared to itself. Wire strings collated against docs/protocolo-ipc-nucleo-sidecar.md sections orden_emparejar/codigo_emparejamiento/acuse_emparejamiento: exact match. Version 4 and the closed 11-type set untouched.

AC-4 bit-for-bit verified: main.rs gains exactly 6 lines (one use plus a 4-line early dispatch) at the top of async fn main(), before Configuracion::desde_entorno(); no existing line changed or reordered; `hexcell` with no args and with any non-'emparejar' argv falls through unchanged; &argumentos[2..] cannot panic for argv len 2.

Credential discipline holds: the pairing value is printed by design, motivo comes verbatim from the sidecar's sanitized field, and no phone number or JID appears in any IPC message, log line, error Display or printed output (adr-0010). No new dependency: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are untouched, no clap, no QR crate; the raw QR string is printed with an honest external-renderer note.

EVIDENCE QUALITY: 05-validation.json records duration_s 0 for all seven commands and paraphrased output_excerpts ('all workspace tests passed') rather than raw tool output. The dispatch report corroborates 7/7 commands, 5 stability reps and a clean -race run, and the test code reads as honest under manual inspection, so this is a reporting-fidelity note, not a fake-green finding.
